To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic intermittent hypoxemia (i.e., sleep apnea) increases sympathetic nerve activity and blood pressure, and this occurs early in the development and is mediated by activation of the hypothalamic PVN.
chronic intermittent hypoxemia activates brain circuits that contribute to the development of hypertension.

chronic intermittent hypoxemia activates brain regions that control blood pressure and body fluid homeostatis, and that these neurogenic responses are evident early during the development of chronic intermittent hypoxemic hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which chronic intermittent hypoxemia (CIH) initiates the development of hypertension.
the mechanisms that underlie sleep apnea-associated hypertension.
the poorly understood mechanisms by which sleep apnea/ CIH initiates hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic intermittent hypoxemia increases sympathetic control of arterial pressure: role of increased neuronal activity in the paraventricular nuclei.
CIH increases the contribution of PVNs to the support of MAP, which is mediated in part via increased sensitivity of Na+/osmosensitive neurons in the PVN to hypertonicity.
chronic intermittent hypoxemia (CIH) increases sympathetic control of arterial pressure (AP) and blood volume (BV) by increasing neuronal activity in the PVN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early neurogenic mechanisms that initiate sleep-apnea/CIH hypertension are complex and include activation of sympathetic outflow and body fluid regulatory neurons.
CIH increases SNA and PVN neuronal activity to support blood pressure.
CIH activates brainstem regions that control SNA and body fluid homeostatic functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CIH increases the contribution of PVH neuronal activity in the regulation of SNA and MAP, even at an early stage of hypertension.

the sympathetic nervous system is activated early in the course of chronic intermittent hypoxemia, and the activation of sympathetic nerves is a major component of the pathophysiological changes associated with the development of sleep apnea/chronic intermittent hypoxia-associated hypertension.
CIH activates neurogenic mechanisms early in its development, which could contribute to the early initiation of CIH-associated hypertension.
